title: Stage supports, don't stack them
statement: Bring each support, such as a word bank, hints or sentence starters, onto the screen only at the step that uses it, so no screen opens on many live targets.
example: An audit of 21 student screen types across four lessons of one course led to the rule that no screen may open on fifteen live targets.
detail: The rule is one of seven in an attention standard that a grade 3 reading course codified from an audit of all 21 student-mode screen types in four of its lessons, measured at two screen sizes with per-element pixel shares and a blurred copy of each screen (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/process/ATTENTION-HIERARCHY.md`, lines 3-11). It has the cloze word bank arm when a blank is aimed at, hints unlock after the first attempt and sentence starters wait behind a request, and the standard treats a screen that can't pass it as not done.

evidence.quote: **Support is staged, not stacked.** Word banks, hints, and sentence starters mount at the step that uses them: the cloze bank arms when a blank is aimed, hints unlock after the first attempt, starters live behind "Need a starter?". A screen must never open on fifteen live targets.
Codified from the WITW UX Attention Audit (2026-08-31; branch `witw-tier3-conformance`), which measured all 21 student-mode screen archetypes
